statement: The tank of a school water cooler is a rectangular box that measures $60$ centimeters long, $30$ centimeters wide and $40$ centimeters tall on the inside. The tank is refilled from bottles that each hold $4$ liters of water. How many full bottles are needed to fill the empty tank completely? ($1$ liter $= 1{,}000$ cubic centimeters)

choices.misconception: I used 100 cubic centimeters per liter instead of 1,000, so I got 720 liters and 180 bottles.
I found the volume, 72 liters, but multiplied it by the 4 liters in each bottle instead of dividing by it.
I divided 72,000 cubic centimeters by 4 without first changing cubic centimeters into liters.

hints: Start with the volume of the tank in cubic centimeters.
Change the volume to liters, then divide by the number of liters that one bottle holds.
The volume is $60 \cdot 30 \cdot 40 = 72{,}000$ cubic centimeters, which is $72{,}000 \div 1{,}000 = 72$ liters.

solutions.reliable: The tank holds $60 \cdot 30 \cdot 40 = 72{,}000$ cubic centimeters, or $72$ liters. Each bottle holds $4$ liters, so it takes $72 \div 4 = 18$ full bottles.
solutions.elegant: Each bottle holds $4 \cdot 1{,}000 = 4{,}000$ cubic centimeters, and $72{,}000 \div 4{,}000 = 18$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
